RESULT
White vitriol crystals were obtained from the mixture of zinc carbonate and magnesium carbonate by different chemical actions followed by filtration and crystallization.
PRECAUTIONS
The precipitation of zinc hydroxide should be complete.
The crystals should not be dried over the Bunsen flame.
The solution should not be overheated during crystallization.
During crystallization, the evaporated solution should be sårred with a glass rod to avoid crust formation.
All the glasswares should be handled with care.
Note:
1. Repeated crystallization can be done to get the pure crystals.
2. A long cooling gives better crystals. Care should be taken that the mother
liquor does not get cooled to contaminate the crystals.

EXPERIMENT NO. 14
Object: TO SEPARATE A MIXTURE OF DYES IN INK BY PAPER CHROMATOGRAPHY AND TO DETERMINE THE Rf VALUES OF
THE DYES.
APPARATUS REQUIRED
Fine capillary tube
1. Beaker (500 ml)
Whatman filter paper
3. Paper clips
5. Pencil and scale
CHEMICALS REQUIRED
1. Black ink
2. Methanol
THEORY

Chromatography is found to be a simple technique to separate various components in a mixture. Chromatography is categorized as paper chromatography, gas chromatography, thin layer chromatography and column chromatography.

The separation of a mixture by paper chromatography is based on the fact that different substances are adsorbed by the cellulose fibres Of the paper to different extents. The components which are more firmly adsorbed on the paper are carried away less nearer across the paper by a moving solvent. On the other hand, the components which are less firmly adsorbed on the paper are carried away more farther across the paper by a moving solvent. In this way, different components in the mixture (here dyes in the ink) become separated in different coloured bands.

The Rf value of a component gives the idea on how firmly it gets adsorbed on the paper. Hence, different substances have different Rf values. The Rf value of a component is given by Distance travelled by the component from the original line Rf = Distance travelled by the solvent from the original line
